description:
A worktree is removed; its BUILD DIRECTORY is not. Measured 2026-08-13 in cuneiform: the main checkout's `core/engine/target` had reached **61 GB across 729,816 files**, and a *warm* `cargo test --no-run` — compiling nothing — exceeded two minutes because cargo stats that tree on every invocation. A single parallel worktree adds another ~7 GB of its own. Nothing collects any of it.

The engine already has the right instinct elsewhere: `chief reap` exists for orphaned agent trees, and `77-reap-by-inherited-run-marker` closed the process half. This is the DISK half, and it is the same shape — chief creates a resource per run and has no matching teardown.

**Do not make this Rust-specific.** The pattern is general: a per-worktree build directory that the language toolchain owns and chief created the conditions for — `target/` (cargo), `node_modules/` (npm/bun), `.venv/` (uv), `build/`. The rule is *what chief created with the worktree goes with the worktree*; what the OPERATOR put there does not.

**The hazard to design around:** a shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` (which cuneiform may adopt) means the build directory is NOT inside the worktree, so a naive `rm -rf $worktree/**/target` either misses it or — far worse — deletes a cache other live runs are using. Detect the shared case and refuse rather than guess.

userStories.title: Removing a worktree removes what chief caused to be built in it
userStories.description: Teardown symmetry: chief created the worktree, so chief collects what accumulated inside it.
acceptanceCriteria: Worktree removal also removes build directories INSIDE that worktree, from a table of known toolchain artifacts (`target/`, `node_modules/`, `.venv/`, `build/`) — a table, so adding a toolchain is a row rather than a new branch.

It removes only what is inside the worktree being removed. A path that resolves outside it — a shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`, a symlink — is REFUSED with the reason stated, never followed. Asserted over adversarial paths in a pure candidate function, the `sweep_candidate` posture cuneiform's cross-system harness already uses.
Reclaimed bytes are reported, so the operator sees what the run cost in disk as well as in tokens.
A worktree chief did NOT create is never touched.

userStories.title: `chief reap` collects the artifacts of runs that already ended
userStories.description: US-1 fixes the future; the fleet already carries the debt. Two empty worktrees plus a 1.4 GB one were found sitting behind finished runs in a single repo.
acceptanceCriteria: `chief reap` gains a disk pass covering build directories under worktrees with NO live registered run — the same liveness rule the process reaper already applies, so it can never touch a running build.
`-n` reports bytes-by-path without signalling, matching the existing dry-run contract.
It is bounded by age as well as liveness, so a worktree between iterations of a live run is never collected.
Mutation-checked: a live run's target directory must survive a reap, and a stale one must not. Recorded in the notes.
